newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing says concessions in best interests of all.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says concessions in best interests of all.

text.p: U.S. airspace giant Boeing Co said on Wednesday it had agreed to certain conditions to meet European Commission concerns regarding its planned merger with McDonnell-Douglas.

"By agreeing to the European Commission's conditions we took the action we believe was in the best long-term interests of our shareholders, customers, our suppliers and the more than 200,000 employees of Boeing and McDonnell-Douglas," Boeing Chairman and Chief Eexecutive Officer Phil Condit said in a statement made available in Brussels.
Condit said the Commission's "positive opinion" on the merger was a significant step towards completing the merger.
Boeing said it had agreed to conditions in several areas to win EU approval for the $15 billion merger:
-- it had agreed to license patents obtained under U.S.-funded defence contracts to commercial aircraft manufacturers on a "non-exclusive, reasonable royalty basis".
-- it had agreed to keep McDonnell Douglas commercial aircraft activities in a separate legal entity for 10 years.
-- it had pledged not to agree any new exclusive supply contracts with commercial aircraft makers until August 1, 2007 except when another manufacturer had offered such an agreement.
-- it had agreed not to enforce the exclusivity provisions in its existing supply agreements with AMR's American Airlines, Delta Air Lines and Continental Airlines.
